name: Forty Years Below - Antartica Show - Fundraiser for Coastguard Mana
venue: Plimmerton Boating Club,66A Moana Rd, Plimmerton, Porirua 5026, New Zealand, Porirua
long_description:
Forty Years Below - Antartica Show - Fundraiser for Coastguard Mana
The rugged beauty of the Old Man Range in Central Otago is a long way from the expanse of Antarctica, but for a young boy Roger Lusby, the two worlds were connected by the sight of American orange tailed aircraft soaring over his parents apricot Orchard and Roxburgh, Central Otago.

These childhood moments sparked a curiosity that lead Roger to spend a year at Scott base in 1969.

Now almost 60 years later he is touring his show called “40 Years Below” to communities who will have the unique opportunity to hear his stories first hand.

Roger offers a glimpse into what it was like to live and work as a base mechanic for a year and Sir Edmund Hillary's original base.

The evening also features are moving trip tribute to Sir Ernest Shackleton's legendary 1914 endurance expedition, celebrating one of histories's greatest stories of survival.

A seasoned balladeer Roger’s audiovisual show includes pictures, stories, songs, poems and humour to share his experience.

All funds collected from Rogers show go to help fund your local community needs.

Feedback from earlier shows.

Enthralling, inspiring, superb. Informative and enlightening.
I felt like I had been to Antarctica.
I have been to many presentations of time spent in Antarctica over the years, but none have evoked such a feeling for the unique place of peace and solitude, yet mixed with extremely tumultuous and unimaginably harsh conditions.

There will be a $15 charge for this show that will be collected in cash at the door.

name: Propagandhi: Australia & Aotearoa Tour 2027 | Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington
venue: 92 Vivian St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011
long_description:
Propagandhi: Australia & Aotearoa Tour 2027 | Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington
Propagandhi will make their long-awaited return to Australia and Aotearoa in early 2027, marking their first shows in the region in nearly eight years.

The ever-evolving standard-bearers of politically charged punk have actively kicked against musical confines and bro-punk conservatism, promoting a message of anti-fascism since 1986. Distilling their DNA of breakneck riffs, hardcore ethos, and radical consciousness, their message remains as vital, and volatile, as ever.

The tour comes in support of the Manitoba, Canada-based outfit’s eighth album, *At Peace*. In true Propagandhi fashion, it’s smart music for dangerous times. “Everything I’m singing about is still coming from being the same person that wrote and sang our first record *How to Clean Everything* in 1993,” Chris Hannah states, recalling the band’s snarky skate-thrash origins. “But what we’re putting into the songs now, probably reflects more despair than 30 years ago when we had similar perspectives, but with strands of hope and naivete. Now it’s the existential dread of eking out a life worth living in this completely failed society.”

Propagandhi are set to bring their incendiary live show back to Australia and Aotearoa, drawing from a body of work that continues to challenge, confront, and inspire.

IHC's Capture the moment
IHC’s Capture the moment 2026 Photography Competition is coming to Waitohi.
Capture the moment is IHC’s photography competition for New Zealanders aged 13 and over who have an intellectual disability or an intellectual disability and autism.

Building on the success of the IHC Art Awards, Capture the moment celebrates creativity through the lens – whether a camera, mobile phone, or tablet.

The competition is a platform for self-expression, confidence-building, and connection, while highlighting the unique perspectives and stories of photographers. It helps raise awareness of the creativity within the IHC community and encourages inclusion and appreciation through visual storytelling.

Our judges select 30 finalists whose work is exhibited at FOTOFEST in the Hawke’s Bay. FOTOFEST is a vibrant, city-wide visual arts and cultural event held across Hastings and Napier, featuring exhibitions in galleries, community spaces, outdoor locations, and local businesses. This year’s theme was ‘Nature: the living world’.
Coming to Waitohi Hub, Johnsonville, Wellington for one month.

long_description:
Historic Petone Walking Tour
Petone is one of New Zealand's oldest European settlements. Come for a walk around central Petone with people who are passionate about its history.

The foreword to Susan Butterworth's 1988 book - "Petone - A History" says "Petone is a colourful place, stamped with the mark of sturdy independence... The years that have gone before have contributed to its sense of identity as a distinctive community". Those years have also left their trace in the places and buildings of central Petone.
The session will cover themes of Petone's early settlement, industrialisation, and the history and development of its historic centre. You will see some of Petone's remaining historic buildings and learn about their past and present uses.

Each tour is limited to 20 people.
Note: The Community House at 6 Britannia Street, one of Petone's listed historic buildings, will be open from 1pm before each tour. People are welcome to have a look around and a Petone Historic Society guide will be on hand to answer questions about the building and its history.

Booking is REQUIRED for this event.
Cost: Free, koha is welcome

Learn more and book on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/historic-petone-walking-tour-2026/

This event is part of the 2026 Wellington Heritage Festival, running 24th October - 15th November. Discover over 160 more events on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Health & Safety:
The walk involves some uneven footpaths and uncontrolled road crossings. Safety advice will be given at the start of the walks.

id: FULLY BOOKED - There’s Gold in Them Thar Hills: Terawhiti Station Tour-Entrance to Terawhiti Station; 220 South Makara Road,900 South Makara Rd, Makara, Wellington 6972, New Zealand, Wellington-All Events In
name: FULLY BOOKED - There’s Gold in Them Thar Hills: Terawhiti Station Tour
venue: Entrance to Terawhiti Station; 220 South Makara Road,900 South Makara Rd, Makara, Wellington 6972, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
FULLY BOOKED - There’s Gold in Them Thar Hills: Terawhiti Station Tour
Discover the rich, though not in gold, history of Mākara's Terawhiti Station during this 4WD guided tour.

"There’s gold in them thar hills!"

That is what hundreds of would be miners thought during the late 19th century on the south western hills of Wellington, but sadly for all their efforts, less than 200 ounces of gold was actually declared.

Terawhiti Station has been one of New Zealand’s oldest and largest sheep stations, located on the southwest coast of Wellington. Today the Station is approximately 4,800 hectares running sheep and cattle, and a home for our esteem Kiwi, running from Te Ika a Maru Bay in the north down to Karori Stream in the south and Cape Terawhiti in the west.

This area has had a rich and varied history. Goldmining was prominent on the Station during the mid to late 19th Century. While payable quartz veins containing gold were located, these seams came to an abrupt end making mining a fragmented and expensive exercise.

The Company that expended the most time and money into Terawhiti Station goldfields was the Albion Gold Mining Company, with its battery built in 1883. It is one of the last remaining remnants of a short-lived gold mining rush.

Come with us under tour leader Michael Grace, a director of Terawhiti Station on a 4x4 owner drive tour to these Station goldmining sites during the Wellington Heritage Festival and in particular stopping to look at the conservation work proceeding to restore the Albion Battery as a future public Education Centre on Terawhiti Station.

The Wellington Goldfields Heritage Society Inc, working closely with historical organisations and others deeply interested in this important piece of New Zealand history is dedicated to preserving, restoring and promoting the 19th century gold mining sites and artifacts on Terawhiti Station.


Vehicles:
Those taking part in the tour must have a 4 x 4 drive vehicle. A maximum of 15 vehicles allowable for the tour. Drivers may be asked if they have space to take passengers who do not have a suitable vehicle to negotiate the roads on the Station.

Payment:
Please pay in advance on line to Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga, coordinator of this event, 030 502 – 0939456-00 with your name in reference and Terawhiti goldfields.
Payment to go to the Wellington Goldfields Heritage Society Inc for conservation work.

venue: 28 Whitehouse Road, Tītahi Bay, Porirua 5022,28 Whitehouse Rd, Titahi Bay, Porirua 5022, New Zealand, Porirua
long_description:
Dungeons & Dragons - An All Ages Adventure
Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?

Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?

Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?

Then All Ages Dungeons & Dragons is for you.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s brand-new space for gamers, Titahi Bay Studios and Lounge, is for you.

Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together.

No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!

This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle), but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.

If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

long_description:
REVERIE
Reverie opens with a mesmerizing, atmospheric work that gently rocks between dream and reality - Hanna Kulenty’s A Cradle Song. The shimmering textures of Adam Schoenberg’s Las Estrellas unfold into a celestial dance, while Leonard Bernstein’s youthful Piano Trio provides a taste of his early brilliance and quirky personality, foreshadowing the irrepressible energy of his later Broadway compositions. A new NZTrio/SOUNZ Tarling Trust commission, Icarus on Titan from Karlo Margetič, situates the trio as explorers on an alien world, before entering a state of Romantic fervour with Schumann’s Piano Trio No. 3, which is brimming with lyrical expression.

Described as a “national treasure” (NZ Herald), NZTrio He Taonga Wairere is renowned for its eclectic repertoire, outstanding talent and warm kiwi stage presence. Bringing together three incredibly accomplished artists: Amalia Hall (violin), Matthias Balzat (cello) & Somi Kim (piano), every NZTrio performance powerfully reaffirms the importance and cathartic nature of a live musical experience in today’s digital world.

Hanna Kulenty - A Cradle Song
Adam Schoenberg - Las Estrellas
Leonard Bernstein - Piano Trio
Karlo Margetić (NZ) - Icarus on Titan (2026 NZTrio / SOUNZ Tarling Trust Commission)
Robert Schumann - Piano Trio No. 3 in g minor

long_description:
FULLY BOOKED - Wellington’s Hidden Brick Making History Revealed
Come and hear the Tonks family story of brick making in Pōneke and its impact on the growth of the capital city.

Hear from Gary Tonks, a descendant of early Wellington settler and prominent businessman, William Tonks, as he shares the story of the brick making industry in Wellington and the impact this had on the growth and prosperity of the capital city from the early 19th century through to the 20th century.

There are many outstanding brick buildings and constructions remaining in Wellington from an industry that peaked in the late 19th century and the early 20th century.

Gary traverses the history of his family’s business and other brick making companies through that time.

long_description:
Korimako Trio

Korimako Trio

Helene Pohl, violin; Rolf Gjelsten, cello; Michael Endres, piano

 

ST ANDREW’S ON THE TCE, NOV 6 AT 7.00PM

The Korimako Trio are celebrating their first anniversary with a wonderful programme to share with you that combines classical elegance with romantic depth, a programme which showcases the warmth and deeply communicative musicianship of these star performers.

The concert opens with Zemlinsky's Trio in D Minor, a late 19th century example of Viennese Romanticism, lyrical, dense and emotionally expressive. This is followed by Janacek’s Violin Sonata (for violin and piano) deeply dramatic with folk elements. A return to Romanticism with Chopin’s Introduction and Polonaise Brillante in C major, for cello and piano follows and the concert concludes with Haydn’s Piano trio in A major (Hob.XV), bright and witty, with plenty of classical charm. A beautifully varied journey through four distinct musical eras, balancing full trio textures with virtuoso duo highlights.

 

Bookings at Humanitix: https://events.humanitix.com/korimako-in-wellington

Admission $50, $40 concession, tertiary students $10 and secondary free.

venue: Samuel Marsden Collegiate School,Marsden Ave, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
From Plate to Page: An Evening with Peter Gordon
Peter Gordon is a chef, restaurateur, writer and fusion pioneer whose eclectic cuisine has had global reach. Join us at this special fundraising event for Katherine Mansfield House & Garden to hear about the books, travel, people and experiences that have shaped his life.

For forty years Peter has gathered ingredients, textures and techniques from around the world and brought them to diners at his award-winning restaurants such as The Sugar Club and The Providores, and into homes through his eight cookbooks. He has cooked for world leaders including Queen Elizabeth II and Barack Obama, presented shows for the Discovery Channel and Whakaata Māori (Māori Television), and appeared on the shows of Nigel Slater and Jamie Oliver in the UK and as a guest judge on MasterChef NZ. He is also the founder of the hugely successful UK charity event Who’s Cooking Dinner? and its NZ equivalent Dining for a Difference.

The evening will begin with a glass of Hunter’s Wines’ award-winning MiruMiru™ and delicious canapés in the foyer (a non-alcoholic option will also be available). We will then move into the auditorium for a conversation with Peter hosted by Katherine Mansfield House & Garden Director Cherie Jacobson.

This event is being held to raise funds for our Category 1 Historic Place and writer’s museum in Thorndon, which is open six days a week. We offer an annual programme of events and activities designed to encourage creativity and we host school and tour groups to share the life, literature and legacy of Katherine Mansfield.

long_description:
Tape Night! with Donna van Talgon, George D Angus, Indigogue Browne
Pyramid Club is happy to present a night of analogue tape misadventures and manipulations.

Donna van Talgon (aka. Izzy Fyfe/youbeepastablaster) is a musician and sound maker from Ōtepoti/Dunedin who uses multi-speed cassette tape transcription machines to warp found cassettes and home recordings. Matt Middleton of Crude fame describes their music as a "Watersian descent into the mind of madness, chronozone. Utter postmodernism, samples from multifarious eras and ethnicities and qualities gratuitously reworked on-a-whim, a mixture of pure noise and cuts of electronic, a juggernaut, a plunderphonic ride into irregularity, dissonance, discord, deconstruction, re-absorption, loops."




George D Angus (aka. Daniel Beban) is a BBC trained tape operator who has several decades of experience in coaxing absurdist sound collages out of reel-to-reel tape machines, including three releases of tape music on Thrill Jockey with Alexander Tucker as Imbogodom.




Indigogue Browne is a multidisciplinary artist and filmmaker producing chaotic semi-improvised sparkly harsh noise-pop and omnichord meanderings.
https://swampsoul.bandcamp.com/album/swamp-soul-one-2



Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.
